alt: Formal education happens in institutions with a curriculum and qualifications; informal education happens through families, peers and media. A staircase shows the levels: nursery, primary, secondary and tertiary. Cards contrast the official and hidden curriculum and note the limits of online learning.
caption: Formal education climbs from nursery to tertiary; informal education happens everywhere.

alt: Four cards. Functionalism: shared values, a bridge to universalistic standards, role allocation and human capital. Marxism: Bowles and Gintis on preparation for work and the myth of meritocracy; Bourdieu on cultural capital. Radical critics: Illich on deschooling, Freire on banking education. Feminisms: gender roles reinforced in school, and Sharpe’s finding that girls’ priorities shifted towards careers.
caption: Each perspective asks whose interests education serves.

alt: A chain: a middle-class home gives knowledge, language and tastes; this cultural capital is what schools value; so middle-class pupils attain more. Schools therefore reproduce class inequality and legitimise it by making it look like individual merit. A note warns that cultural capital is not money.
caption: Schools reward middle-class culture, then call the result merit.

alt: Four numbered steps: a teacher labels a pupil as less able; gives them easier work and less attention; the pupil sees themselves as less able and stops trying; low attainment fulfils the expectation. A note adds Rosenthal and Jacobson’s field experiment, Becker’s ideal pupil and the point that pupils can reject labels.
caption: Label, treatment, self-image, outcome: one mark for each link.

alt: Six cards: the ideal pupil (Becker), stereotyping, the halo effect, positive and negative sanctions, pro-school subcultures that value achievement, and anti-school subcultures such as Willis’s lads. A note adds that racism and sexism work through labelling, low expectations, harsher sanctions and an ethnocentric curriculum.
caption: Interactionists look at the small, everyday processes that shape pupils.

alt: Nested boxes. Inside school: labelling, setting and streaming, subcultures and ethnocentric curricula. Outside school: material factors such as poverty, cultural factors such as cultural capital, and home and community factors such as parents’ support. Class, gender and ethnicity intersect.
caption: Explain attainment gaps from both inside and outside the school gates.
